Dashboard Audit and Polish: Before and After

The proposed website Dashboard (/website/dashboard?version=proposed), 6 Oct 2026. Before is feat/dashboard-proposed at d89f3927; After is feat/dashboard-audit-fixes. Same width (1440px, or 390px for the phone pair), same data. The dashboard stays as colourful as the live site.

Opening summary panel

Before
Blue panel with five figures; three of them (9 Cr, 11 Cr, 14,757) repeat the scholarship cards directly below; one label ran two labels together
After
Same blue panel, with the NMBA figure and the one Department figure no section prints (₹67,977 Cr), its label and source on separate lines
Why
Nothing is said twice on one screen; the panel stays as colourful as before.

Scholarship cards

Before
Coloured cards; rupee figures in 12px type; trend lines with no years
After
Same colours; rupee figures at reading size; first and last year under each line and a dot on the latest point
Why
The dot ties "74.23 lakh students in 2025-26" to its point; years tell a ten-year line from a ten-month one.

Hostel and Top Class Education cards

Before
Coloured cards; trend line with no years
After
Same colours; years and latest-point dot on the line
Why
As above.

Scheme portal cards, and their place on the page

Before
After the funds section. NMBA repeated 34.83 Cr; its map was a picture only. SMILE carried an extra trend line; Senior Citizens repeated the spending chart
After
Straight after the Department's results. NMBA keeps its map, now clickable: choosing a State/UT switches the whole page to it, and its four other figures sit beside it. SMILE keeps its funnel; Senior Citizens says its spend in one sentence; DAPSC's trend has years
Why
Results are read together; the map does a job instead of repeating the State/UT section; colours unchanged.

Year by Year Trends

Before
Curved lines; year labels tilted
After
Straight lines; year labels flat
Why
Each figure is one a year — a curve draws values nobody reported; tilted text is slower to read.

Year on Year Report

Before
Bars and a line on two different axes in each card; no headline figure
After
One measure at a time on one axis with a switch; each subtitle states the latest year (e.g. "2025-26: 3,700 Seats")
Why
Where a line crosses a bar on two scales means nothing but reads as a finding; the subtitle gives the answer the chart supports.

Fund Release and Expenditure

Before
"FUNDS" label repeating the heading; spending chart includes DAPSC (a cross-Ministry allocation) and short codes (IPSrC, RVY); date 30.09.2026
After
Heading alone; the Department's own components by full name; 30 Sep 2026
Why
Like is compared with like, and a citizen can read every row.

Choosing a State (Kerala shown)

Before
Most sections stayed All-India with no warning except one line under Scholarships
After
One line under the picker names which programmes publish figures for the State; each All-India section carries an "All-India Figures" badge
Why
Choosing Kerala and seeing five of seven sections unchanged read as a broken picker.

Data Source of Each Indicator (Ministry and Division view only)

Before
A full section at the bottom of the dashboard
After
A one-line link at the bottom, opening its own page with a way back. Citizens never see either
Why
It reports on the data pipeline, not on the schemes (your decision).

Phone, opening panel (390px)

Before
Five figures in the panel
After
Two figures; same blue
Why
Less to scroll on a phone before the first card.

Not Changed, and Why

ItemReason
Every figure, label and titleAs the API, the Department's file or the live site gives them. Data points are noted in Figma.
ColoursKept, as on the live site: each scheme and portal card's own colour, and the blue panel. Ambedkar stays blue rather than the live site's red, which means "rejected" on this estate.
Chart cards elsewhere on the siteUnchanged. Only this page uses the flat (outlined) chart card.
Geographic India mapNot part of this branch: it arrives with the Bharat maps work (PR #707).
